parts.text:
Haemoglobin is described as having quaternary structure.
State what is meant by quaternary structure.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The effect of the partial pressure of oxygen ($p\text{O}_2$) and the effect of the partial pressure of carbon dioxide ($p\text{CO}_2$) on the percentage saturation of haemoglobin was investigated.
A sample of mammalian blood was exposed to a gas mixture that contained increasing $p\text{O}_2$. In the experiment, the $p\text{CO}_2$ was maintained at $2.7\text{ kPa}$. The percentage saturation of haemoglobin in the blood sample was determined as the $p\text{O}_2$ increased.
The experiment was repeated with further samples of blood with a $p\text{CO}_2$ maintained at $5.3\text{ kPa}$ and at $10.7\text{ kPa}$.
The results are shown in Fig. 6.2.
{{figure:figure_6_2.png}}
Fig. 6.2
parts.text:
The $p\text{CO}_2$ of alveolar air is $5.3\text{ kPa}$.
With reference to Fig. 6.2, state the likely partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli of the mammal.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the range of partial pressures of oxygen in respiring tissues **and** use Fig. 6.2 to give evidence for your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the information in Fig. 6.2 to describe the effect of increasing $p\text{CO}_2$ on the percentage saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: State the name given to the effect you have described in part **(iii)**.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Explain the advantage to the mammal of the effect you described in part **(iii)**.
